meta.title: KVMFlow
meta.description: Control a real computer through an IP-KVM, record HID actions with before/after screenshots, turn a recording into an editable YAML workflow, and replay it with a verified state machine. Open the KVMFlow panel from the left sidebar icon, or dock the same panel as a tab in the right sidebar to watch the target while chatting. In the panel you manage devices, watch the live screen, record steps, edit workflows, and supervise runs. Tools exposed to the agent cover snapshots, keyboard, mouse, text, visual verification, recording, workflow generation, and run control. BIOS workflows arm a HID hotkey before you press the target's power button, then continue once the video signal appears. Radxa Linkr is supported through its public HTTP API; other KVM models remain a driver-extension point. Recording and run artifacts are stored under DSH_HOME/kvmflow (configurable with dataDir). When a non-16:9 target leaves black bars in the capture, KVMFlow detects the target area, draws its outline, keeps the mapping per device, and converts panel clicks, kvmflow_mouse, and workflow click actions into the target screen automatically; a pointer readout and a mapping toggle let you verify or override it. Real-time video over WebRTC is available when the device web account is configured: the Host relays the WHEP signaling and the browser decodes the H.264 stream peer to peer, with automatic fallback to JPEG polling.
